newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra says Q1 sales hit by stockpiling.
newsitem.headline: Astra says Q1 sales hit by stockpiling.

text.p: Swedish drugs company Astra said on Monday that its sales and earnings in the first quarter of 1997 were hit by stockpiling prior to the end of 1996, especially in Sweden.
Astra reported sales of 10.13 billion crowns in the first quarter compared to 9.34 billion crowns in the same period a year earlier, which was a nine percent rise.
Pre-tax profit edged up one percent to 3.46 billion crowns from 3.44 billion crowns.
"Sales development during the first quarter of 1997 was affected by a certain amount of patient and wholesaler stockpiling prior to year-end 1996, especially in Sweden," Astra said in a statement.
"The above mentioned stockpiling has also impacted earnings."
Astra had been expected by the market to post a pre-tax profit of 3.93 billion crowns, a Reuters poll found.
Astra's sales of blockbuster anti-ulcer agent Losec rose 14 percent during the first quarter to 4.80 billion crowns from 4.21 billion.
Total world Losec sales amounted to about 7.05 billion crowns from 5.90 billion a year earlier.
